title: Custom Signs. Made for Your Space.
intro: From a distinctive logo to the finished installation. Explore the light, material and character of your next sign.

sections.title: Front-Lit Channel Letters
sections.intro: A defined illuminated face brings your business name into view. A starting point for shopfronts and commercial façades where the lettering needs a clear presence.
features: Illuminated letter faces
Light is directed through the face, with the sides giving each letter its depth.
Face & return finishes
Review the face colour, side finish and letter depth around your logo.
Mounting to suit the frontage
Discuss individual fixings or a carrier with your installer, along with power and cable access.
sections.custom: Logo, overall size, face colour, return finish and light colour.

sections.title: Backlit & Halo-Lit Letters
sections.intro: An opaque face and a halo of light create a softer dimensional effect. The wall becomes part of the appearance, making this a considered choice for brand feature walls.
features: Rear illumination
Light spreads behind the letters while the visible faces remain visually calm.
Metal face & finish
Explore brushed, painted or plated appearances against your brand and interior palette.
The wall shapes the halo
Wall texture, colour and stand-off distance affect how the glow is seen.
sections.custom: Logo proportions, metal appearance, light colour and wall clearance.

sections.title: Metal & Dimensional Letters
sections.intro: Let the material do the work. Unlit dimensional lettering brings texture and definition to a wall, with an appearance that changes with the surrounding light.
features: Cut or built-up construction
The artwork and required depth guide the fabrication approach.
A finish with character
Discuss brushed, polished, painted or other available surfaces using a finish reference.
Dimension without integral light
The sides and shadows reveal depth; daylight and site lighting remain part of the design.
sections.custom: Metal direction, surface finish, letter depth, size and fixing approach.

sections.title: Acrylic Letters & Logo Signs
sections.intro: A clean outline and a deliberate use of colour turn your artwork into a dimensional sign. Explore solid, clear or layered appearances for a distinctive brand wall.
features: Colour & transparency
Review opaque, translucent or clear material directions for the intended effect.
Depth & layered details
Thickness, stacked shapes and visible edges give the logo its dimensional character.
Lighting is a separate choice
This concept is unlit. If you want illumination, we review a construction designed for that effect.

sections.title: Lightbox Signs
sections.intro: An illuminated panel carries your logo or graphic inside a defined housing. Use the face, shape and viewing direction together when planning a storefront or projecting sign.
features: A panel for logos & graphics
The illuminated face gives the design a continuous display area.
Single or double-sided direction
Compare wall-facing and projecting arrangements for the directions people approach from.
Housing & support
Review the cabinet depth, frame finish, bracket and local fixing requirements as one assembly.
sections.custom: Face shape, graphics, cabinet finish, overall size and mounting arrangement.

sections.title: Neon-Style Light Signs
sections.intro: Illuminated lines follow your lettering or graphic to create a focal point. A different direction from a lit panel, suited to expressive wording and simple logo outlines.
features: Line-based artwork
Curves, stroke spacing and small details are reviewed at the intended sign size.
Light colour & visual rhythm
Choose the illuminated colour and discuss how separate lines or sections work together.
Backing & cable arrangement
Review a clear or coloured backing, visible fixings and the power-supply location.
sections.custom: Wording, logo outline, light colour, backing shape and hanging or fixing method.

sections.title: Specialty Custom Signs
sections.intro: For a reference that does not fit a standard letter style, start with the effect you want. Explore marquee lettering, visible light points and combinations of shape, material and light.
features: A design-led construction
The artwork, scale and intended effect guide the fabrication review.
Light points or mixed materials
Discuss the spacing of exposed lights, dimensional forms and surface combinations.
Resolve the details early
Confirm fixing, component access, location and the supplied scope before production approval.
